newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks lower in morning, more weakness seen.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks lower in morning, more weakness seen.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were lower in Wednesday morning trade, dragged down by losses in the property sector, with dealers forecasting more weakness during the day.
"It goes lower. The futures say that," said one dealer.
The Hang Seng index was trading 83.16 points lower at 13,320.13. Turnover was HK$3.45 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.
The market quickly lost an early boost that came on news of CITIC Pacific's HK$16.25 billion acquisition of a 20-percent stake in China Light and Power Co Ltd, dealers said.
China Light was trading up HK$1.00 at HK$34.70 while CITIC Pacific was off HK$0.70 at HK$38.80.

Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities, said the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's recommendation on Tuesday that the maximum loan to value ratio for properties of over HK$12 million in value should be reduced to 60 percent had hit the property sector. The ceiling had been 70 percent.
"This latest policy should not translate into any concrete or damaging impact on the market. But people sense that this is a signal from the authorities to curb speculative activities," Chan said.
"If the situation persists, they ... can tighten the policy on other medium or small size properties. People are a bit cautious about the implications of the latest measures."
Hong Kong's property sub-index was off 320 points, or 1.24 percent, at 125,508 as property stocks fell across the board.
Cheung Kong (Holdings) was down HK$1.50 at HK$73.25, Henderson Land sank HK$2.00 at HK$72.75 and Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$1.25 at HK$89.50.
Futures also suggested the Hang Seng index would fall further, dealers said, with January Hang Seng futures off 104 points at 13,261 before expiry on Thursday.
Among active issues, HSBC Holdings was up HK$0.50 at HK$175.00 after its U.S. subisidary reported a 34-percent increase in 1996 earnings to US$380 million.
Leading Spirit fell HK$0.145 to HK$1.93. It said it plans to issue 300 million new shares to chairman Wong Shi Ling at HK$1.95 per share.
